Includes a full-body exfoliation, warm oil massage, scalp and hand treatment, and a quiet rest with tea and something small to eat.

blogs.title: Why your skin barrier matters more than any serum
blogs.excerpt: If your skin stings, flakes and reacts to everything, the answer is almost never a stronger product. It is usually a quieter routine.
blogs.content:
Most of the skin concerns I see in the treatment room are not caused by a lack of products. They are caused by too many of them, used too often, in the name of doing something.

## What the barrier actually is

The outermost layer of skin — the stratum corneum — is often described as a brick wall. Skin cells are the bricks, and between them sits a mortar of lipids, ceramides and cholesterol. When that mortar is intact, water stays in and irritants stay out.

When it is compromised, everything feels like a lot: water stings, cream burns, and skin looks red and tight even when it is dry.

## The usual culprits

- Daily exfoliation with acids, sometimes twice
- Hot showers and foaming cleansers
- Retinoids started too fast, with no buffer
- Layering five actives in one evening

> Skin is not a problem to be solved. It is a system to be supported.

## A quieter week

If your skin is in that reactive place, try seven days of this:

1. A cream or balm cleanser, removed with lukewarm water.
2. One hydrating serum, applied to damp skin.
3. A moisturiser with ceramides, morning and night.
4. SPF in the morning, every morning.
5. Nothing else. No acids, no scrubs, no new products.

Most people notice a real shift by day five. If things are still angry after two weeks, that is the point to book a skin consultation rather than buy another bottle.

## What comes after

Once the barrier is calm, you can reintroduce one active — one — at a low frequency. Two nights a week, buffered over moisturiser, for a month before increasing. Slow is not a lack of ambition. It is how skin actually changes.
blogs.author: Shelley

blogs.title: The case for slowing down your evening
blogs.excerpt: Sleep is not a switch. It is a slope, and most of us are trying to go from full speed to flat in four minutes.
blogs.content:
We talk about sleep hygiene as if it were a checklist: no screens, cool room, eight hours. All of that helps. But the piece most people skip is the transition — the twenty minutes where the body is told, gently, that the day is closing.

## The nervous system needs a runway

Your body shifts from sympathetic (alert) to parasympathetic (rest) through signals: warmth, dim light, slow breathing, familiar scent, the absence of decisions. Without those signals, you can lie in a dark room with your heart still at a hundred beats a minute.

## Three things that work

### Warmth, then cool

A warm shower or bath an hour before bed, then a cool bedroom. The drop in core temperature is one of the strongest sleep signals we have.

### Scent as a cue

Use the same oil or balm each evening — on wrists, or a drop on the pillow. After two weeks the scent itself starts to do the work.

### A low-stakes ritual

Not journalling your life goals. Something small: five slow breaths, a stretch on the floor, one page of fiction. The point is repetition, not depth.

> The goal is not to fall asleep faster. It is to stop arriving at bed already braced.

## What to skip

The temptation is to add a supplement, then another. Before you do, give yourself two weeks of the same three cues, at the same time, and see what changes. Bodies respond to consistency far more than intensity.
blogs.author: Shelley

blogs.title: What actually happens in your first skin consultation
blogs.excerpt: No pressure, no ten-step plan. Here is exactly how the first forty-five minutes go — and what you leave with.
blogs.content:
If you have never had a proper skin consultation, the idea can feel intimidating — as though you will be assessed and found wanting. It is the opposite. The whole point is to leave with fewer things to worry about, not more.

## Before we begin

Come with a clean face if you can, and bring the products you are currently using. Photographs of the labels are fine. Knowing what your skin has been through is more useful than any single product.

## The conversation

We start with history: what has changed, what has been tried, what your skin does after a bad week. We talk about your cycle, your sleep, your work, because skin is not separate from any of it.

Then we look — under daylight and under a lamp — at texture, hydration, pigmentation and barrier.

## What you leave with

- A short explanation of what your skin is doing and why
- A routine of no more than four products
- A realistic timeline, usually 8–12 weeks
- A written plan, sent by email the same day

## What we will not do

We will not sell you a course you do not need, and we will not promise you different skin in a week. What we can promise is honesty about what is achievable, and a plan that fits the life you actually have.

Each guest receives a skin reading and a 20-minute bespoke mini-facial during the session, plus a printed guide to take home.

Limited to 10 people. Bring your current products if you would like them reviewed.

No booking required, though taster slots fill quickly. Tea and pastries from the bakery next door.
